fact: Central Bank of Libya circular 9 of 2026 allows licensed electronic payment companies to issue e-wallets to legally resident foreigners, and its Banking and Monetary Control Department will inspect the companies for compliance.
The Central Bank of Libya directed commercial banks by letter of 4 March 2026 to activate the LYPay instant payment system in their banking apps for QR-code purchases at POS devices by 8 March.
The Central Bank of Libya says it runs the LYPay and OnePay instant payment services, launched in 2024, and will raise their transfer and purchase limits.

The Central Bank of Libya regulates mobile and e-wallet payment by circular: Circular 9/2026 of 11 March 2026 sets e-wallet rules for banks, Moamalat and e-payment companies, with compliance checked by field inspection by its banking and currency supervision department.
